Definition: linsey-woolsey, i.e. cloth of linen and wool carded and spun together
BiblicalUsage: Sha'atnez is cloth of linen and wool together, and the law forbids it twice: thou shalt not wear a garment of divers sorts, as of woollen and linen together; and neither shall a garment mingled of linen and woollen come upon thee.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mingled garment is the picture of a mingled life: God keeps His people's cloth unmixed, because He keeps His people unmixed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
